title: The Boy Named After a Dog: The Extraordinary Journey of Magil Babi Ngathin
subtitle: A personal history of a Murle boy whose name was connected to a protector dog, his childhood in Manyath, and the journey that shaped his life.
author: Babi Magil

body.heading: The Child Who Was Welcomed by a Protector
paragraphs: In the peaceful lands of Murle, where the morning begins with the sound of cattle bells, birds singing, and mothers preparing the first meal of the day, a child was born.
It was the 1970s. A time when life in the villages was simple.
There were no hospitals nearby. No machines to check the health of a newborn. No modern technology to announce the arrival of a child.
Life depended on family, elders, experience, and the relationship between people, animals, and the land.
In those days, a child's story did not begin with a hospital record. It began with the community. It began with nature. It began with signs.

body.heading: The Child Who Received a Name From a Guardian
paragraphs: His mother was known as Keda. His father was Babi Ngathin, a respected man from the Nyeriza generation.
When the child was born, nobody knew that his name would come from an unusual visitor.
In Murle homes, dogs were not just animals. A good dog was a companion, a protector, a hunter, and a member of the homestead.
This particular dog was special. It was known for hunting and protecting the family.
On the day this child entered the world, the dog came close. Instead of running away, it approached the newborn. It laid beside him and licked him gently.
The people watching saw something special. The dog had accepted the child. The child had been welcomed by a protector.
And from that moment, the name Magil was born.

body.heading: Growing Up in Manyath: The Fearless Boy
paragraphs: Magil grew up in Manyath village.
Like many Murle children of his generation, his childhood was surrounded by cattle, family, nature, and village life.
The village was not rich in money, but it was rich in experiences.
The cattle camps were their schools. The elders were their teachers. The forests and rivers were their adventure.
But among all the children, young Magil had something that made people talk about him.
He was fearless, especially when it came to snakes.

body.heading: The Day a Child Chose a Different Path
paragraphs: For young Magil, a life-changing moment came when he was only 13 years old.
The country was passing through difficult times. War was affecting many communities.
In Murle land, young people were being taken by soldiers known as Koliyam.
Some joined willingly. Others were taken by force.
Families lived with fear and parents tried to protect their children.

body.heading: The Boy Who Left Manyath
paragraphs: Despite his young age, Magil made a decision. He wanted to join the Koliyam.
His family did not support the idea. They tried to stop him.
But Magil had already made up his mind.
He secretly left and travelled toward Pibor.
The place where many young recruits gathered was Lukurnyang.

body.heading: The Tears of a Mother and Father
paragraphs: When Magil's parents discovered that he had left, they followed him.
They found him in Lukurnyang and begged him to return home.
Families could arrange the release of their children by giving cattle.
His parents were ready to do whatever they could.
But Magil refused. His mind was already set.
His parents left with tears, praying that God would protect their son.

body.heading: The Journey Into Uncertainty Begins
paragraphs: The journey was filled with hardship.
There were no comfortable vehicles, no easy roads, and no guarantee of tomorrow.
Many people died along the way.
Some died from diseases such as malaria and typhoid.
Some became lost and never returned.
Some drowned while crossing rivers toward Ethiopia.
Friends who laughed together before the journey became memories along the road.

body.heading: Arrival in Boma and the Separation
paragraphs: After many difficulties, they reached Boma.
The young people were separated.
The younger ones were sent for education and training at Dimma camp in Ethiopia.
For a village boy who grew up with cattle and open land, entering a camp was a completely different world.
Now he had to learn books, pens, classrooms, rules, and discipline.

body.heading: The Boy Who Sold Firewood for Education
paragraphs: School required materials. Pens, books, and basic supplies.
But Magil did not have money.
He collected and sold firewood to get what he needed for education.
A boy who once followed cattle was now carrying firewood to build his future.
The same determination that made him leave Manyath was now helping him survive Dimma.
